question: Pushkar Camel fair is associated with which of the following states?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Rajasthan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Camel Fair

 
 
• ​Every year the famous Camel Fair is organized in Pushkar city of Rajasthan.
 
• The celebration goes on for 5 long days.
 
• The Fair is generally organized in October or November.
 
• The special attraction of the fair is the challenging Camel Race.
 
• Other famous events include tug of war between teams and also competition for the longest moustache.
 
• Locally called Kartik ka Mela or Pushkar ka Mela.
 
• The Fair takes place on the bank of Pushkar Lake which is also an important pilgrimage site.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other Festivals of Rajasthan
 
 
• Teej Festival

 
 
• ​Teej is a famous festival widely celebrated in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan.
 
• Teej is also celebrated in other states of India(Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhatisgarh, etc.).
 
• Teej festival is celebrated in July or August.
 
• Festival is named after insects 'Teej' and women offer food to them so they don't come out of their homes.
 
• Festival celebrated by women to celebrate a happy union of marriage and fasting to pray to Lord Shiva and Parvati.
 
• Women engaging in fun activities like singing, dancing, and a swing ride under the tree. 
 
 
 
• Desert Festival
 
 
• ​Every year the Desert Festival is organized in Sam Sand Dunes of Jaisalmer Desert.
 
• The celebration goes on for 3 long days.
 
• The Festival is generally organized in February.
 
• Desert festival is organized by the Rajasthan Tourism Development Authority.
 
• The Festival is a complete fusion of music dance and Mr Desert competition.
 
 
 
• BrajHoli
 
 
• ​Every year BrajHoli is celebrated in the Braj region of Rajasthan(Bharatpur).
 
• Celebrated in March and a few days before Holi.
 
• The special attraction of the festival is the Rass Leela dance by local people.
 
• The dance depicts the love story of Radha-Krishna.
 
• People also consume bhang and thandai as popular drinks.
 
• The Festival is full of cultural activities and colourful events.
